title: Weighing of the own mark and of the bond against the grip, oscillator cells

key_results.statement: For every grip, the source term $g_sq_{x_s}$ is removed by the unitary shift $q\to q+\phi$, $\phi(x)=-g_sG(x-x_s)$: it enters the eigenvalues only through the shifted grips $F(q_{x_i}+\phi(x_i))$ and the body-independent constant $-\tfrac12g_s^2G(0)$ (uncompressed contract, $M\to\infty$ first).

At first order in $g_s$, every weight is $\partial_cX[F_c]\,\Delta\phi$ for $X\in\{\text{cost},C^{(1)},C^{\rm mark}\}$, and $\rho_{\rm mark}=\partial_c\ln C^{\rm mark}/\partial_c\ln C^{(1)}$, independent of the places and of the distance to the source; cost, $C^{(1)}=\mu\langle F\rangle_0$ and $C^{\rm mark}$ are fixed by the total contracts with and without the body.

Field constants $G$, $w_0$, $g_r(\nu)$, $c_r(\tau)$ and $J_n(\mathbf r)=\int_0^\infty c_r^n d\tau$, with $J_1=G/2$, $0<c_r\le c_0\le w_0$, $J_n(\mathbf r)\le w_0^{n-1}J_1(\mathbf r)$, $J_2\le w_0G_0/2$.

Made field at $\lvert d\rvert\gg1$, $L\gg\ell$: $G$ is linear, logarithmic ($K_0$) or $1/(4\pi\kappa_h\lvert d\rvert)$ for $D=1,2,3$ below $\ell=\sqrt{\kappa_h}/m_h$ and decays as $e^{-\lvert d\rvert/\ell}$ above it.
For (G2), a lowest eigenvector exists in the limit $M\to\infty$ iff $1+2\sigma M_kF_2G_0>0$; otherwise the lowest eigenvalue of $C_M$ tends to $-\infty$.

For (G2), exactly: cost $=\mu F_0-\mu^2F_1^2G_0/(2D_\mu)+Z(2\mu F_2)$, $C^{(1)}=\mu(F_0+F_2w_0)$, $C^{\rm mark}=-\mu^2G_0(F_1^2+\zeta)/(2D_\mu)<0$, with $D_\mu=1+2\mu F_2G_0$ and $Z(a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\ln(1+ag(\nu))d\nu$.

Zero-point part of the (G2) mark: $\zeta=\frac{4F_2^2}{\pi G_0}\int_0^\infty g^2(1+2\mu F_2G_0)\chi(2\mu F_2g)d\nu\ge0$, $\zeta=(4F_2^2J_2/G_0)[1+O(\mu F_2G_0)]$, strictly increasing in $\sigma M_kF_2$ for $F_2\ne0$.

For (G2), exactly at first order in $g_s$: $\Delta W=\mu F_1\Delta\phi/D_\mu$, $\Delta W^{(1)}=\mu F_1\Delta\phi$, $\Delta W^{\rm mark}=-2\mu^2F_1F_2G_0\Delta\phi/D_\mu$; the zero-point part is not weighed.

For (G) with finite Gaussian variance of $F$, at order $\theta^2$: $C^{(1)}=\mu\langle F\rangle_0$ exactly and $C^{\rm mark}=-\mu^2S$, $S=\sum_{n\ge1}a_n^2J_n/n!$, $a_n=\langle F^{(n)}(q_x)\rangle_0$.
For (G) at order $\theta^2$: $\Delta W^{(1)}=\mu a_1\Delta\phi$ exactly and $\Delta W^{\rm mark}=-2\mu^2T\Delta\phi$, $T=\sum_{n\ge1}a_na_{n+1}J_n/n!$.

Bond profile at order $\mu_1\mu_2$: $U(\mathbf r)=-2\mu_1\mu_2\sum_{n\ge1}a_n^{(1)}a_n^{(2)}J_n(\mathbf r)/n!$; for (G2) $U=-\mu_1\mu_2[F_1^{(1)}F_1^{(2)}G(\mathbf r)+4F_2^{(1)}F_2^{(2)}J_2(\mathbf r)]$.

Bond weight for a common grip: $\Delta W_{\rm bond}=-2\mu_1\mu_2(\Delta\phi_1+\Delta\phi_2)T(\mathbf r)$ with $\Delta\phi_1+\Delta\phi_2=2m_{\mathbf r}\Delta\bar\phi$; for $d\gg\lvert\mathbf r\rvert$, $m_{\mathbf r}-1=O(\lvert\mathbf r\rvert^2/d^2)$ below $\ell$ and $(\mathbf r\cdot\hat d)^2/(8\ell^2)$ above; reference to a body gives an error of first order in $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert/\min(d,\ell)$.
For (G2), exactly: $U=U_{\rm cl}+Z_b$ with $U_{\rm cl}=-\tfrac12v^T\mathbb Mv$, and $\Delta W_{\rm bond}=-(2F_2/F_1)\sum_i\Delta\phi_iv_i(\mathbb Mv)_i$; the zero-point bond $Z_b$ is not weighed.

At order $\mu^2$, for every grip: $\rho_{\rm mark}=\rho(0)$, $\rho_{\rm bond}=m_{\mathbf r}\rho(\mathbf r)$, $\rho(\mathbf r)=2a_0T(\mathbf r)/(a_1S(\mathbf r))$, the same for every level and both branches and independent of the distance to the source; excluded: $\langle F\rangle_0=0$, $\langle F'\rangle_0=0$, $\Delta\bar\phi=0$.
For (G2), exactly: $\rho_{\rm mark}=4F_2\langle F\rangle_0/(F_1^2+\zeta(\sigma M_kF_2))$.

For (G2), exactly: $\rho_{\rm bond}=\frac{4F_2\langle F\rangle_0}{F_1^2+\zeta_b}\sum_iw_i\Delta\phi_i/\Delta\bar\phi$, $\zeta_b=4F_2^2J_2(\mathbf r)/G(\mathbf r)[1+O(u)]$; the bond is weighed at $\sum_iw_ix_i$, the midpoint for equal labels.
For grips with $F(0)\ne0$, $F^{(n)}(0)=O(F(0)\beta^n)$, $\varepsilon^2=\beta^2w_0\ll1$, at order $\mu^2$: $\rho(\mathbf r)=2F(0)F''(0)/F'(0)^2+O(\varepsilon^2)$ uniformly in $\mathbf r$.

At order $\mu^2$ and leading order in $\varepsilon$, $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ and $\rho_{\rm bond}=m_{\mathbf r}$ for every level and both branches, at every distance and separation, on all three graphs and all $L,\kappa_h,m_h>0$ with $\varepsilon,u\ll1$, iff $2F(0)F''(0)=F'(0)^2$ (square grip $F=F(0)(1+\beta q)^2+O(q^3)$; in (G2) $4F_0F_2=F_1^2$).

Square (G2) grip at order $\mu^2$: $\rho(\mathbf r)=(1+\beta^2w_0)/(1+\beta^2J_2(\mathbf r)/G(\mathbf r))$, so $\rho_{\rm mark}-1=\beta^2(w_0-J_2/G_0)\in[\beta^2w_0/2,\beta^2w_0)$ and $\rho_{\rm bond}/m_{\mathbf r}-1\to\beta^2w_0$ for $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert\gg\ell$, up to $O(\varepsilon^4)$; level dependence at relative order $\varepsilon^2u$ for the mark and equal-label bonds.

No (G2) grip gives $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ exactly for every level and both branches; at order $\mu^2$ no (G2) grip gives $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ and $\rho_{\rm bond}=m_{\mathbf r}$ where $J_2(\mathbf r)/G(\mathbf r)\ne J_2/G_0$ (all $\lvert\mathbf r\rvert\gg\ell$); a (G) grip of fixed shape with $F(0)\ne0$ has $\lvert\rho_{\rm mark}\rvert\to\infty$ as $\theta\to0$ unless $T_f=0$.

In the (G2) eigenvector with one quantum in the uniform mode the weights are unchanged, $\rho_{\rm mark}=4F_2(\langle F\rangle_0+F_2/(N_fm_h))/(F_1^2+\zeta_1)$ with $\zeta_1-\zeta=O(F_2^2)$, and the criterion (2.18) is unchanged.

definitions.name: made field of the held source
Gaussian averages of the grip derivatives
bond weighting of the two bodies
grip variation over the zero-point spread

open_issues: Level dependence of ρ_mark beyond order θ² obtained only for (G2), through ζ, not for a general grip.
Fields of 06-ilang-source and 07-ilang-weight, m_h = 0 with an anchor, and the formation speed are outside this package.
Whether the square grip or the tuned grip 4F₂⟨F⟩₀ = F₁² + ζ is selected by anything in the language is not addressed (item 6, M10).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of costs, weights, ratios and the small parameters ε², u
The (G) formulas at order θ² reduce to the order-μ² terms of the exact (G2) formulas, and the linear grip gives ρ = 0 in both
Square grip at tree level: the shifted cost μF(c)/D_μ is proportional to F(c), consistent with (2.15) at w₀ = ζ = 0
